title: Managed Identity vs Service Principals
description: Compare managed identities and service principals to decide which identity model fits your Azure application.

data.text: Two Ways to Authenticate Azure Resources
Both managed identities and service principals are identities in Entra ID, but they solve different problems. Service principals require you to manage credentials. Managed identities do not.

cards.title: Managed Identity
cards.description: Azure-managed identity with no secrets to store or rotate.

cards.title: Service Principal
cards.description: App registration-based identity with client credentials.
pros: Full control over certificates and secrets
cons: You must protect the client secret or certificate
Secrets expire and must be rotated

rows: You manage client secrets or certificates

data.title: Recommendation
data.text: Use managed identities for code running in Azure. Use service principals only when you need to run outside Azure, such as in GitHub Actions or local development.

The real difference is who owns the credential. A service principal authenticates with a client secret, certificate, or federated credential that you configure. A managed identity is a service principal whose credential is created and rotated by Azure and exposed only to the resource it is attached to. Both are Entra ID identities; both need role assignments.
Workload identity federation closes the gap

Historically, anything outside Azure needed a service principal secret. Federated credentials changed that. GitHub Actions, Azure DevOps, and AKS can present a short-lived OIDC token that Entra ID exchanges for an access token. You still use a service principal, but there is no secret to rotate, which removes most of the operational advantage of managed identity.

data.title: GitHub Actions authenticating without a secret
data.content: The workflow requests an OIDC token, and azure/login exchanges it for an Azure token using the app registration federated credential.
data.code:
permissions:
  id-token: write
  contents: read

jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: azure/login@v2
        with:
          client-id: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CLIENT_ID }}
          tenant-id: ${{ secrets.AZURE_TENANT_ID }}
          subscription-id: ${{ secrets.AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID }}
      - run: az webapp deploy --resource-group rg-shop --name shop-api --src-path app.zip

data.title: What interviewers look for
data.text: If asked "managed identity or service principal?", answer with the environment first: inside Azure use a managed identity; outside Azure use a service principal with federated credentials; only fall back to a secret when the platform cannot federate. Mention that a managed identity is still a service principal under the hood.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Managed identities are simpler and more secure for Azure-native workloads.
Service principals are necessary for non-Azure environments.
You can use both: a service principal for local dev and managed identity in production.
